model_type: Book-value compounding (BVPS growth x exit Price/Book) with dividend income, discounted at Cost of Equity -- NOT a free-cash-flow DCF

valuation_philosophy.methodology: General Capital is a non-bank deposit taker (NBDT): its subsidiary General Finance Limited funds a property-secured first-mortgage loan book with retail term deposits. This model values GEN's EQUITY DIRECTLY via book-value compounding: intrinsic value = PV of projected dividends per share (Years 1-5) + PV of a Year-5 exit value equal to projected Year-5 book value per share x an assumed exit Price-to-Book multiple, both discounted at Cost of Equity (CoE). This is the same family of model used elsewhere in this repo for depository/insurance institutions (SOFI, SRBK, FRFHF, FIH.U).
valuation_philosophy.why_not_fcf_dcf: Free cash flow is deliberately BLANK in GEN.NZ_Metrics.csv and must stay that way. Reported operating cash flow for a growing NBDT is dominated by loan origination and deposit-book flows, not owner earnings: FY2026 net cash used in operating activities was NZ$(24.6)m -- driven by NZ$92.0m of net new loan advances only partially offset by NZ$63.2m of net new deposit receipts -- in a year the company reported a healthy NZ$2.72m NPAT. FY2025 OCF was the mirror-image +NZ$41.4m when deposit growth briefly outpaced loan growth. Neither figure says anything about distributable value; both are pure funding-flow artefacts of balance-sheet growth timing. A standard unlevered FCF DCF applied here would show the company perpetually 'burning cash' in growth years and 'gushing cash' in slower years, which has no relationship to intrinsic value. There is also no meaningful enterprise-value/net-debt bridge for a deposit taker: customer term deposits (NZ$248.1m gross at FY26) are the funding base of the lending business, not financing debt to net against equity value, so TotalDebt is reported as 0 and no net-debt subtraction is applied anywhere in this model -- the equity is valued directly.
valuation_philosophy.capital_constraint: A lender cannot grow its book faster than its capital base allows without diluting shareholders. FY2026 equity grew only ~7% (NZ$29.24m to NZ$31.30m) while total assets grew 30% and gross loans grew 63% -- funded by capital ratio headroom above the 8% trust-deed minimum, not by proportionate equity growth. This model's growth driver is therefore the SUSTAINABLE book-value growth rate implied by ROE x (1 - payout ratio), not the (much faster, capital-constrained) loan-book growth rate management is guiding to for FY27 (27.8% loans / 34.6% deposits). If the company grows the balance sheet faster than retained earnings support, it will either draw down capital-ratio headroom (a limited, one-time lever) or eventually need a dilutive equity raise (likely below book, given the current 0.76x-0.88x P/B) -- this model assumes NO new equity issuance and flat share count, i.e. growth financed purely by retained earnings, which is the conservative, non-dilutive base case.
valuation_philosophy.sbc_treatment: Stock-based compensation is confirmed NIL for General Capital (verified from the FY2026 annual report; the only warrants on issue lapsed unexercised in FY2025). No SBC adjustment is required or applied on either the earnings or the share-count side of this model.
valuation_philosophy.roe_vs_coe: The central fact this valuation must confront: GEN's FY2026 ROE (~9.0% on average equity) sits well below both the Cost of Equity built up below (~16.75%) and management's own 17.3% pre-tax discount-rate assumption used in the FY2026 Finance-CGU goodwill impairment test. Under the standard justified-P/B identity, P/B = (ROE - g) / (CoE - g); with ROE 9.0%, sustainable growth g 5.4% and CoE 16.75%, the theoretically fair P/B is only ~0.32x, i.e. roughly NZ$0.11/share on FY2026 BVPS of NZ$0.3406 -- materially BELOW even this model's bear-case output. The market's current ~0.76x-0.82x P/B is therefore not obviously a mispricing; it likely already embeds some expectation of a partial ROE recovery. This model's base case does NOT assume ROE recovers to CoE -- it holds ROE roughly flat around 9%, consistent with four consecutive years of ROE decline (11.9% -> 9.0%) and costs (personnel +39.6%, ECL charge +34%) outrunning revenue growth in FY2026 despite a 63% loan-book expansion. A negative base-case upside is an accepted, and in this case likely correct, conclusion -- consistent with prior negative-base-case precedents in this repo (AGL.NZ, BIT.NZ).

inputs.roe_fy2026_note: NPAT NZ$2.724m / average total equity NZ$30.27m (simple average of FY25 NZ$29.24m and FY26 NZ$31.30m closing equity), per Analysis.json valuation_framing.
inputs.net_debt_note: Not applicable. Customer term deposits (NZ$248.1m gross at FY26) fund the loan book and are the raw material of the lending business, not financing debt; no net-debt bridge is used anywhere in this equity-value model.
inputs.sbc_source: Verified NIL -- FY2026 annual report confirms no stock-based compensation; the only warrants on issue lapsed unexercised in FY2025.
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: No SBC, no announced buyback program, no equity raise assumed. Share count held flat at 91.877912m across all scenarios; growth is financed entirely from retained earnings (see valuation_philosophy.capital_constraint).

cost_of_equity.coe_rationale: Built up from a risk-free/ERP base plus four explicit micro-cap/sector premiums: (1) NZ risk-free rate ~4.25% + equity risk premium ~6.0% = base CAPM cost of equity 10.25%. (2) +2.25pp micro-cap illiquidity premium (market cap ~NZ$23.9m, well under the ~NZ$300m liquid-microcap threshold used elsewhere in this repo). (3) +1.75pp extreme shareholder-concentration/thin-float premium (top holder 34.5%, top 5 holders 66.4%, top 20 holders 88.6% of shares on issue -- a genuinely illiquid, closely-held register). (4) +1.25pp credit/property-cycle premium (76% Auckland concentration in a soft, uncertain NZ residential market, unseasoned FY2026 loan-book vintage growing 63% in a single year). (5) +1.25pp regulatory transition-risk premium (Deposit Takers Act 2023 capital-standard consultation ongoing through 2026, full implementation ~2028, a live risk to the minimum capital bar a small NBDT like General Finance must clear). Total: 16.75%. This lands just below management's own 17.3% pre-tax discount rate used in the FY2026 Finance-CGU goodwill impairment test -- a powerful independent anchor from the company's own valuation work, and this model deliberately does not use a cost of equity materially below it.
cost_of_equity.management_anchor_source: FY2026 annual report, Note 10 goodwill impairment testing, Finance CGU pre-tax discount rate.

historical_growth.restatement_note: FY2019-FY2024 EPS and per-share figures are restated x4 (and share counts /4) to the post-1-for-4-consolidation basis (executed 2-Aug-2024) for comparability. Cross-check: restated FY2024 EPS = 0.72c x 4 = 2.88c, versus the company's own FY2025 annual report restatement of 2.90c -- a close match confirming the x4 restatement is correct.
historical_growth.operating_income_note: 5yr CAGR (FY2021-FY2026) is inflated by the low FY2021 COVID-era base (op income only NZ$2.35m); the 3yr figure (FY2023-FY2026, 14.5%) is a cleaner recent trend, and both are loan-book-growth-driven, not applicable as the DCF driver (see growth_rate_source).
historical_growth.npat_note: NPAT 3yr CAGR of only 6.45% against a 14.5% operating-income CAGR over the same period is the key divergence signal: costs (personnel +39.6%, ECL +34%, amortisation of intangibles roughly 7x) are outrunning revenue growth, and FY2026 NPAT actually FELL 2.9% YoY despite a 63% loan-book expansion. The 5yr NPAT CAGR is a meaningless artefact of the near-zero FY2021 base (NZ$0.082m) and should be disregarded.
historical_growth.eps_note: Restated EPS 3yr CAGR is NEGATIVE (-8.8%, FY2023 3.92c to FY2026 2.97c) -- consistent with the ROE-decline story below. The 5yr figure is another near-zero-base artefact (FY2021 restated EPS only 0.20c) and is not usable.
historical_growth.bvps_note: Book value per share (restated) grew a steady 7.8-8.5% over 3 and 5 years -- driven by retained earnings compounding, the most reliable and least distorted of the CAGR series here because it is a stock (level) measure less sensitive to a single low-base year than the flow (NPAT/EPS) measures above.
historical_growth.roe_trend_note: ROE on average equity has declined every year for four straight years (11.9% -> 9.0%), the single most important fact for this valuation. The base case explicitly does NOT extrapolate the historical BVPS CAGR (7.8-8.5%) forward, because that CAGR was earned at higher, now-declining ROE; instead growth is derived from a forward sustainable-growth formula (ROE x (1-payout)) applied to the current, lower FY2026 ROE.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: sustainable_growth_roe_x_retention -- ROE(FY2026, ~9.0%) x (1 - 40% payout ratio) = 5.4% per year. This is the maximum book-value growth rate financeable from retained earnings alone without diluting shareholders via a below-book equity raise or drawing down capital-ratio headroom indefinitely -- deliberately NOT the loan-book growth rate (management guides 27.8% FY27 loan growth, moderating to 20-35%), which would require either continued capital-ratio drawdown or new equity.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Operating-income CAGR (14.5% 3yr) diverges sharply (>30% relatively, and in direction) from the selected book-value growth driver (5.4%) and from the negative EPS CAGR (-8.8% 3yr). This divergence is not a data error -- it is the central thesis of this valuation: a rapidly scaling balance sheet (loans +63% FY26) is not translating into proportionate profit or per-share value growth because costs are outrunning revenue and capital constraints cap how fast book value can compound without dilution.

base.rationale: ROE stabilises just below its FY2026 level (~8.7-9.0%) rather than recovering -- consistent with four straight years of ROE decline and FY2026's demonstrated pattern of costs (personnel, ECL, amortisation) outrunning a genuinely fast-growing revenue line. Book value compounds at the resulting sustainable retained-earnings rate (~5.2-5.6%/yr, averaging 5.4%), with 40% of NPAT paid out as dividends per the company's stated policy. Exit at 0.80x book -- the middle of the stock's actual recent post-consolidation trading range (0.74x-0.88x observed FY2025-FY2026) -- reflecting a going-concern that continues to earn sub-cost-of-equity returns and is priced by the market accordingly, neither a re-rating nor a further de-rating assumed.

bull.rationale: Operating leverage finally arrives: cost-to-income improves as the FY2026 loan-book vintage seasons without credit deterioration, the Equifax Positive outlook converts into a rating upgrade (lowering marginal funding cost), and the Research & Advisory drag disappears. ROE recovers toward 12-13% by Year 5 -- still below management's own 17.3% CoE anchor for the Finance CGU, so this is a genuine but not heroic recovery, not a re-rating to cost-of-equity parity. Exit at 1.10x book reflects the market beginning to price in the recovery; cost of equity is modestly lower (15.5%) reflecting reduced credit/execution uncertainty once the growth vintage has seasoned cleanly.

bear.rationale: Credit costs normalise as the unseasoned FY2026 vintage (loans +63% in one year against a soft, Auckland-concentrated NZ property market) matures and the ECL charge rises faster than net interest income; cost-to-income stays elevated as compliance/regulatory-transition costs under the Deposit Takers Act 2023 land on a still sub-scale cost base. ROE compresses to ~7%. Exit at a steeper 0.60x book discount, near the low end of the stock's observed post-consolidation range, reflecting a market that has lost confidence in the growth-into-profitability story; cost of equity is modestly higher (18.0%) reflecting realised credit-cycle and regulatory stress.

justified_pb_check.note: This formula-based fair P/B (0.32x, ~NZ$0.11/share) sits BELOW even this model's bear-case IV (NZ$0.1449, implying ~0.43x P/B at exit). The gap exists because the justified-P/B formula assumes ROE and CoE persist unchanged in perpetuity with zero mean reversion, whereas the DCF-style model above prices a finite 5-year path plus an exit multiple set from the stock's own actual recent trading range (0.60x-1.10x across scenarios) rather than a theoretical steady-state number. Both signals point the same direction: the current NZ$0.26 price is not obviously cheap on a book-value basis given ROE well below cost of equity, and a materially positive base-case return requires either an ROE recovery this model's base case does not assume, or the market continuing to pay a premium to formula-fair value that it has arguably already been paying (current 0.76x-0.82x P/B versus 0.32x formula-fair).

entry_price.methodology: Entry = PV(base-scenario DPS Years 1-5, discounted at 15%) + PV(base-scenario Year-5 exit value at the CoE-derived exit price, discounted at 15%). Note CoE (16.75%) exceeds the 15% hurdle here, so discounting the same exit value at the lower 15% hurdle rate mechanically produces a HIGHER present value than the CoE-discounted intrinsic value above -- entry price sits above (not below) base-case IV, the correct and expected result whenever CoE > hurdle rate.

base.note: Entry price (NZ$0.22) is below the current NZ$0.26 quote but above this model's CoE-discounted base intrinsic value (NZ$0.2054) -- an internally consistent result of CoE (16.75%) exceeding the 15% IRR hurdle, not an error. A buyer paying NZ$0.22 today and exiting at the base-case Year-5 value of NZ$0.3533/share (0.80x projected book) while collecting the projected dividend stream earns approximately a 15% annualised return.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = Cost of Equity (CoE, +/-2pp around the base 16.75%), Columns = Exit Price-to-Book multiple (+/-0.2x steps around the base 0.80x) -- the correct second axis for a bank/NBDT book-value model, in place of WACC/terminal-growth for an FCF DCF. Matrix computed on the BASE-case ROE/payout/BVPS path over 5 years.

probability_weighted.note: Bear weighted above the standard 25% (at 30%) because four consecutive years of ROE decline and FY2026's demonstrated pattern of cost growth (personnel +39.6%, ECL +34%) outrunning a genuinely strong 16.4% revenue increase is an actual trend already in the data, not a hypothetical risk -- this is closer to the base case than a tail scenario. Bull is correspondingly underweighted (20%) because it requires an operating-leverage inflection that has not yet appeared in five years of results. The weighted intrinsic value of NZ$0.2082 implies roughly 20% downside to the current NZ$0.26 quote.

income_framing.note: Given the base case's modest and possibly negative price return, the realistic investment case for GEN.NZ at NZ$0.26 is income plus slow book-value compounding, not capital appreciation. FY2026 DPS was NZ$0.0118 (NZ$0.0033 interim + NZ$0.0085 final), a gross yield of approximately 4.5% at the current price. Dividends are fully imputed under the company's stated policy (FY2026 imputation credits attached: NZ$273,371) -- for a NZ resident taxpayer on the top marginal rate, grossing up for imputation credits raises the effective pre-tax-equivalent yield meaningfully above the headline 4.5% cash yield. This is a small-cap NZ income holding with book-value growth optionality attached, not a growth story; investors expecting multi-bagger upside from the loan-book growth rate (27.8%+ guided for FY27) are very likely to be disappointed given the capital constraint described in valuation_philosophy.

sanity_check.sbc_note: SBC verified NIL (only warrants lapsed unexercised FY2025) -- no SBC adjustment applied to either implied or historical multiples.
sanity_check.consolidation_adjustment: Yahoo Finance's monthly close-price history for GEN.NZ is a raw, UN-adjusted series -- it shows no retroactive split adjustment around the 2-Aug-2024 1-for-4 consolidation date (e.g. Jul-2024 close NZ$0.30 to Aug-2024 close NZ$0.26, a normal small move, not a ~4x jump/drop). Because the raw reported share count for FY2019-FY2024 in the CSV is also on the pre-consolidation (larger) basis, computing historical P/B and P/E using RAW price x RAW shares for each fiscal year-end is internally consistent and requires no further x4 adjustment to the price series itself (a stock consolidation does not change market capitalisation, so price x shares is invariant to it as long as both are drawn from the same historical basis).

implied_multiples.ev_ebitda_note: Not meaningful for a deposit-funded lender.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.pb_pre_consolidation_note: TREATED AS AN OUTLIER, NOT USED. GEN.NZ is an extreme micro-cap with a closely-held register (top holder 34.5%, top 5 = 66.4%) and thin free float; pre-consolidation P/B multiples of 3.3x-5.8x on a company earning single-digit-to-low-teens ROE are not credible efficient-market pricing -- they reflect illiquid price discovery on low trade volumes (tens of thousands of shares/month) with a handful of marginal buyers/sellers setting the tape, not a market clearing price for the whole company. These multiples are excluded from the historical average used for the sanity check, consistent with the instruction to use the post-consolidation era as the reliable anchor.
historical_averages_ex_outliers.pb_post_consolidation_note: This is the reliable historical anchor: two clean fiscal year-ends (31-Mar-2025 and 31-Mar-2026) post-consolidation, both showing the stock trading at a discount to book consistent with sub-cost-of-equity ROE. Matches Analysis.json's independently-stated 0.76x-0.88x range using 2026 trading prices.
historical_averages_ex_outliers.pe_note: P/E history is not a useful cross-check pre-FY2025 given the EPS restatement and small, volatile absolute NPAT base in early years; post-consolidation P/E was approximately 7.6x (FY2025: 0.235/0.0309... actually price/EPS) to 9.4x (FY2026), broadly consistent with a company earning a mid-single-digit ROE spread below its cost of equity.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/B on the base-case intrinsic value (0.603x) is BELOW the reliable post-consolidation historical average (~0.78x) and below the current actual traded P/B (0.76x-0.82x) -- the model does not require any multiple expansion versus recent trading history to justify its (negative) base-case output; if anything it is more conservative than where the stock currently trades. Implied P/E (6.92x) is below the post-consolidation historical range (7.6x-9.4x). Base-case upside is negative (-21.0%), so the 'price in upper half of historical range with positive model upside' trip condition is moot by construction. The pre-consolidation P/B outliers (3.3x-5.8x) were correctly excluded rather than averaged in, which would have wrongly inflated the historical benchmark and made the negative base case look artificially cheap by comparison.
sanity_check.methodology_note: A book-value-compounding model with an exit P/B anchored to the stock's OWN observed post-consolidation trading range (0.60x-1.10x across scenarios) was used from the outset, which structurally prevents both the peak-FCF-extrapolation failure mode this check targets and the pre-consolidation price-history artefact from contaminating the valuation.
